modality_preference.survey_note: REACH MSNA AAP factsheet, South Kivu and Tanganyika, data June-Aug 2022 (published Sep 2022), N=974 aid-receiving households of 9,889 surveyed; multi-response. No national or 2025 modality preference figure found: REACH 2025 North Kivu key-informant factsheet [s11] is indicative only and its preference chart was not legible. HNRP 2026 (GTS, Minova): 83% of respondents preferred cash transfers over other aid, followed by food and water (43%); single locality, not national.

cwg.name: Cash Working Group (national plus provincial groups: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Tanganyika)
cwg.evidence_note: CashCap (NORCAP) programmatic co-chair post in Goma, 12 months from April 2026, reporting to GiveDirectly [s5]; four provincial groups, MEB and transfer-value harmonisation under way [s4]; latest 4W on ReliefWeb page is Dec 2024 [s7]. Congo Cash Consortium (DRC-led, with GiveDirectly) operates in Masisi [s6].

ai_summary.headline: MPC is the one cash line that kept its 2026 budget, and it is about half funded.
ai_summary.narrative: The 2026 HNRP sought USD 1.4bn at launch for 7.3M prioritised people [s1]; requirements were later revised to USD 2.13bn and FTS shows about 54% funded [s2][s3]. Multi-purpose cash is a separate cluster at USD 110.5M, 5.2% of the revised plan (7.1% at launch), with USD 16.3M received on FTS's single-cluster view, about 15% of its requirement (USD 52.4M, 47%, if shared-cluster flows are counted) [s3]. The CWG reports MPC was the only sector to keep its 2026 budget [s4]. Coordination looks relatively strong: OCHA and GiveDirectly co-lead, with a CashCap co-chair deployed from April 2026 and four provincial groups [s4][s5]. Cash delivery in the east is also run through a DRC-led consortium including GiveDirectly in Masisi [s6]. Evidence on preferences is old and subnational: in South Kivu and Tanganyika in 2022, 70% of households named cash among preferred modalities [s8]. Pooled fund top-ups in September 2026 were partly earmarked to keep cash transfers going [s9]; the MPC share is not visible. This appears to be a plan where cash is protected but where evidence on cost efficiency and feasibility is thin.
barriers: Ongoing conflict and access limits in the east, and funding gap of roughly USD 1bn on the revised plan [s9]
No recent national modality preference data found
Sectoral cash and vouchers not visible in FTS, so total CVA share is unknown
Two inconsistent FTS cluster views make MPC funding hard to state precisely
opportunities: CashCap co-chair and GiveDirectly programmatic lead give the CWG capacity to push MEB harmonisation
Pooled fund top-ups with a cash-maintenance intent could be tracked as MPC share by cluster

total_funding_usd.note: All incoming funding to the plan, pledges excluded. Matches the FTS plan summary.

mpc_usd.note: FTS single-cluster view of the Transfert d’espèces à usages multiples cluster; shared-cluster view US$16.3M. Incoming flows, pledges excluded.

ctp_usd.note: All flows tagged 'Cash transfer programming (CTP)', inside or outside the MPC cluster.

sectoral_cva_usd.note: Flows whose FTS modality field is 'Cash transfer programming (CTP)' and whose destination cluster is not multi-purpose cash: 57 flows. The CTP tag is set by the reporting donor or agency and is not applied consistently, so this is a floor, not a measure of sectoral cash. Largest: Sécurité alimentaire US$9.9M, Protection US$1.4M, Réponse multisectorielle aux réfugiés US$0.4M.

cva_usd.note: Union of the MPC cluster and the CTP tag. Widest defensible FTS cash figure; still a floor because untagged sectoral cash is invisible.

cva_pct_of_total.note: cva_usd as a share of total plan funding.

sectoral_cva_pct_of_total.note: sectoral_cva_usd as a share of total plan funding.

mpc_pct_of_total.note: MPC cluster funding as a share of total plan funding (single-cluster view).

fts_cva.caveat: FTS records funding, not transfers to people, and only to first-level recipients. Sectoral cash depends on a modality tag that reporters apply unevenly.

cva_to_local_pct.note: Indicator 4.2 proxy. Share of FTS cash funding (MPC cluster or CTP tag, US$29.0M) whose first-level recipient is a local or national NGO/CSO or a national government body. FTS does not see sub-grants, so this understates money that reaches local actors through international intermediaries.

all_funding_to_local_pct.note: Share of all plan funding whose first-level recipient is a local or national actor (US$1.8M). Same first-level caveat.

cbpf_cva_to_local_pct.note: Second-level view: share of the pooled fund's cash grants (US$96.8M) that went to local or national actors. Pooled-fund grants are the one onward layer FTS records.

cbpf_all_to_local_pct.note: Share of all pooled-fund grants inside the plan (US$383.2M) to local or national actors.

localisation.caveat: FTS sees first-level recipients only; indicator 4.2 as defined (direct donor allocation to local partners) is therefore a floor. Chair roles come from public CWG pages and may be out of date.
